answer: Anchor an identity's weight to a hash-linked log of its own attested actions across epochs, its voyage. Weight stays at zero until that cumulative, non-backfillable log crosses a fixed participation ridge; only past it does the identity harbor influence. Each epoch entry must be countersigned live by existing peers and cannot be pre-dated or transferred, so a Sybil operator cannot clone one aged log onto many addresses. Every fake must independently repeat the full multi-epoch voyage, so attack cost scales linearly with identity count and never pools into one cheap purchase.
